Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. Follow on X Multiple Authors Oct 2, 2026, 11:00 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and moneylines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 4. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props Bowen's Game of the Week New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills (-6.5, 48.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park, New York Josh Allen and the Bills split their series with the Patriots last season. Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire The Buffalo Bills , the AFC favorite to reach the Super Bowl, will host last season's AFC Super Bowl representative, the New England Patriots , in a matchup of AFC East rivals Sunday. The Patriots will need game plan answers on both sides of the ball to counter the Bills' high-scoring offense, and they'll have to create a more defined passing game without A.J. Brown (ankle) on the field. I like the Bills to win and cover in this one, and in a divisional game with this level of coaching and familiarity, I'll take the under on the total. Let's check out both clubs, and I'll add some props at the end to play, too. NFL betting • Best bets for Sunday: Cincy in danger? • Burrow passes Allen as MVP fave | Odds • Why Lawrence is the best MVP value • Betting favorites go 14-1 in Week 9 • Odds for Week 10 games | Early bets • Super Bowl odds: Jaguars move up • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Bills have the ball: In their Week 3 win over the Chargers, the Bills failed to control offensive tempo, and they turned the ball over. It happens in this league. But don't let one game change the narrative on an explosive Bills offense leading the NFL in scoring (33.7 PPG) and producing top-10 numbers in both passing and rushing. Quarterback Josh Allen will see heavy single-high coverage from New England (both man and zone), which creates opportunities for the Bills to scheme for crossing concepts and big-play throws on deep over routes, and they can also attack the seams with tight end Dalton Kincaid . The man matchup to watch to here is DJ Moore against Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), if the Patriots corner is up for the game. Best versus best. And let's not forget the offensive balance the Bills have with running back James Cook III , who has produced back-to-back games with at least 135 yards rushing, against a New England defense allowing 4.8 YPC. The question I always have for teams versus Allen, given his dual-threat ability, is how much man coverage can you play? And what is your answer for Allen as a runner in the low red zone? Let's see how the Patriots counter, as Allen has rushed for two scores in all three games played this season. He's the league's ultimate difference-maker. When the Patriots have the ball: Quarterback Drake Maye has made some reckless decisions with the ball, throwing a league-high six interceptions and registering a 45.9 QBR (25th in the league). But I'm not going to put this all on Maye, as the Patriots' wide receiver group is lacking juice and matchup edges. With Brown on IR, who is the boundary X to win the one-on-ones? The tape shows us that the New England wideouts aren't creating separation at a high rate. The key here is for Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels to scheme more defined throws -- while having answers to pressure -- versus a Bills defense that has been more zone-heavy (65.9% of opponent dropbacks). Maye is going to see split-safety coverage. Lift the safeties here and create those middle-of-the-field voids for the quarterback to drive the ball. More importantly, the Patriots need to generate some run-game efficiency with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to get the Bills out of two-deep coverage. The Patriots are averaging 3.9 YPC (20th in the league) with an explosive run rate of 8.2% (25th). No question on the numbers here. They are down. Let's see how McDaniels game-plans for Jim Leonhard and the Bills' new defensive scheme to get his QB rolling again. And it wouldn't surprise me if the Patriots try to muddy this one up with a ball control/play-action script. Now, let's get to some prop bets ... James Cook III is coming off two straight big rushing performances and is averaging 6.0 YPC. AP Photo/Adrian Kraus James Cook III rushing yards OVER 88.5 (-111) As mentioned, Cook has rushed for 135-plus in two straight, and he's averaging 19.3 carries per game. Plus, Cook has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season. Take the steady volume and the explosive-play ability here. Hunter Henry receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-110) Henry has topped the 31-yard mark just once this season, and he was held to just one reception in the Week 3 loss to Jacksonville. However, I see the tight end as an answer to the two-high zone coverage of the Bills. Henry can be the outlet for Maye, while also pressing the seams. DJ Moore receptions OVER 3.5 (-133) The juice isn't friendly on this one, but that's a low reception total for Moore. In the two full games Moore has played (he left Week 2 early with an injury), he had at least five receptions in both. Look for the Bills to use motion to deploy Moore, getting him free access off the ball versus man coverage. Matt Bowen 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Moneyline 1-2 -1.1 Spread 6-3 +2.3 Total 1-8 -7.1 Passing props 0-2 -2.0 Receiving props 4-7 -3.4 Rushing props 5-4 +0.4 Rushing and receiving props 1-2 -1.1 Touchdown props 2-6 -1.1 Teasers 3-0 +2.1 Parlays 0-1 -1.0 Overall 23-35 -11.9 Solak's plays Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has produced 463 total yards this season and could be in for another big game Sunday. Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire Detroit Lions -3.5 (-112) at Carolina Panthers It's important to watch the forecast for this game as we get closer to kickoff. There's a good chance of rain showers Sunday night, and we know that Jared Goff 's performance as a passer can be impacted more by bad weather, given his smaller hands. But I still feel comfortable taking this bet at this number because of the Panthers' injury issues. Both starting cornerbacks are expected to miss this game, which all but precludes Carolina from playing man coverage against Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams . If the Panthers take a zone-heavy approach, expect Jahmyr Gibbs to run wild -- heck, expect Gibbs to run wild anyway, as the Panthers are giving up more rushing yards per game to running backs than any other defense. Have I mentioned the Panthers' passing defense is also among the league worst against tight ends? The Lions have Carolina outgunned offensively, and I'm not sure Bryce Young can keep scoring pace. Receiver Jalen Coker (quad) is questionable, three starting offensive linemen ( Ikem Ekwonu , Damien Lewis and Taylor Moton ) are out, and a key backup ( Monroe Freeling ) is in concussion protocol. Detroit's defense is extremely gettable through the air, but the Lions have enough pass rush power to generate sacks and turnovers such that the Panthers can't keep this shootout within one score. Los Angeles Rams -3 (-115) at Philadelphia Eagles Editor's Picks Top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 4 Mike Clay NFL Week 4 betting: Odds, lines and totals for every game Early bets for Week 4: Four games to target right away ESPN 2 Related I would only take this line at -3 (up to -120) and not buy the hook, so move quickly here. DeVonta Smith missed practice Thursday with his hamstring injury, which officially moves him into the "seriously questionable" category as we approach Sunday. I already leaned to the Rams' side with a healthy Smith. If he can't go, the Eagles' receiver corps will feature Dontayvion Wicks , first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown against the loaded Rams secondary. Remember, pass-catching tight end Dallas Goedert is also out with a knee injury. The Eagles' defense had a brutal night last Monday against the Chicago Bears ' passing attack, regularly suffering communication issues as the Bears sent receivers in motion. They get another motion-heavy passing attack in Sean McVay's Rams offense, which gets Puka Nacua back at a critical time -- at 1-2, the Rams need a road win to prevent the sirens from screaming in their Super Bowl-aspiring season. They also have a vengeance play here, as they gave up a big second-half lead to the Eagles last season ... then lost the game on a would-be game-winning field goal that was blocked by Jordan Davis . The Eagles simply have too many personnel deficiencies to ignore against a team as deep and talented as the Rams. Get this line before Smith news pushes it higher before kickoff. Miami Dolphins team total points UNDER 13.5 (-115) Minnesota Vikings DC Brian Flores is calling defense for the first time against his old team. He has downplayed the importance of facing Miami, but I'd imagine the leaders in the locker room know how big of a game this is for their top-flight coordinator. I also think this is about as big of a mismatch as we will see this season. The Dolphins are without running back De'Von Achane , who provided much-needed game-breaking ability from the running back spot. Without him, the Dolphins' best chance for chunk gains will come from the passing game, which is a scary proposition against Flores' blitz-heavy approach. Bobby Slowik, the new offensive coordinator in Miami, lost his job in Houston in large part due to predictable protection rules that were easily exploited by opposing defensive coordinators -- and no coach has been better attacking the Mike Shanahan system in pass protection than Flores. I'm tracking under 13.5 at -115 for a full unit and under 7.5 points at +285 for a half unit. A shutout at 13-1 would be fun, but that's too short of a price to take seriously. Omarion Hampton rushing yards UNDER 45.5 (-109) NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Hampton's share of carries took a hit last week, as he saw 57.7% of the designed rushes after holding 76.7% and 75.0% in the first two weeks of the season, respectively. The Los Angeles Chargers wanted to get Keaton Mitchell more involved as they looked for any sort of juice on offense, and it was a better day for the running game overall. I expect a time share moving forward. But it will be a tough test against the Seattle Seahawks , who boast the best run-defending line in football. There might be no greater mismatch in Week 4 than the Chargers' interior offensive line against defensive tackles Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams . If the Chargers are to find any success on the ground, they'll need to get the ball to the boundary -- those are the Mitchell plays, not the Hampton plays. The Chargers were able to run the ball a lot more last week as they tripped into an early lead after the Bills' many turnovers, but it's more likely they get stuck in a trailing game script in this one. Hampton has big-play ability if he breaks into space, so taking the under on attempts might be a safer approach. I didn't want to pay the juice at under 13.5 attempts at -123 as of this posting, but if under 12.5 appears, I'll be interested in taking that. Kaleb Johnson rushing attempts OVER 8.5 (-115) The Green Bay Packers ' lack of a handoff game is harrowing. Through three games, the Packers have 146 total rushing yards from running backs -- eighth fewest for a team through three games over the past six seasons. The one-dimensionality on offense particularly haunted them against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night, but they've had a long week to explore offensive line reinforcements and recommit to the rushing attack. Green Bay has the fifth-highest pass rate over expectation per Next Gen Stats. Behind that offensive line? No shot. They need to find a rushing attack, and they know it. Critically, the Packers draw a rookie UDFA quarterback ( Jalon Daniels ) making his first career start for a bad Tampa Bay Buccaneers team. The potential to build an actual lead and salt it away should also increase the total handoffs in this game. The Packers clearly don't trust MarShawn Lloyd as a ball carrier, and Chris Brooks is the third-down back. If the running game plays a bigger role this week in a leading game script, Johnson is the most likely beneficiary. I prefer Johnson's attempts to his yardage totals, simply because the Packers' line is still a problem. But both are bettable as his role expands. Woody Marks rushing yards OVER 33.5 (-114) NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks Our Dan Graziano reported this week that his sense of the Houston Texans ' running game is that more work should go Marks' way . I'm inclined to agree. David Montgomery is a good stay-ahead-of-the-sticks rusher, but with Houston's offensive line issues, he has been unable to solve their short-yardage problems on his own. By getting the ball to Marks on the outside, the Texans can find bigger runs without worrying as much about their interior offensive line play. The Dallas Cowboys have given up 114.3 rushing yards per game to running backs through three weeks, fifth worst in the league. They have played three mobile QBs ( Jaxson Dart , Jayden Daniels , Lamar Jackson ) who make run defense more challenging, but the eye test confirms the liability of players like outside linebackers Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku in setting a hard edge. With Nico Collins back in the starting lineup for Houston, the temptation is to think the Texans will become more pass-heavy -- but their offensive philosophy this season was always to give C.J. Stroud a better running game. I'd take Marks to 36.5 this week, and I'd look at some longest rush props as well. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Zay Flowers receiving yards OVER 66.5 (-110) I had all sorts of Flowers overs to target against the Cowboys last week, but his hamstring injury limited him to just 15 routes. Of course, he still went over his yardage prop with 84 yards on only 15 routes. Flowers is a huge-play star-in-the-making in this Declan Doyle offense, and the books still haven't caught up. Flowers has now only played 1.5 games of football through three weeks, and four of those six quarters were with load management. Yet, he has 234 receiving yards and a whopping 9.36 yards per route run because of how easily the Baltimore Ravens are getting him open with motion, backfield alignment and play-action pass fakes. He's as central to this passing attack as Jaxon Smith-Njigba is to Seattle's, and as he strings together full healthy games, we'll never see a number in the 60s for him again. If you're worried about continued management on the hamstring injury, especially in a game the Ravens might dominate, consider taking Flowers' first-quarter receiving props (over 14.5 receiving yards is +100) to ensure the Ravens are still in their base offense. Michael Mayer receiving yards OVER 21.5 (-116) In Brock Bowers ' first game back healthy, Mayer's route share was totally unaffected. Mayer ran a route on 71% of the Las Vegas Raiders ' dropbacks in Week 1, 72% in Week 2, and 70% in Week 3. That's because the Raiders are using Bowers like a true wide receiver. They were in multiple-TE sets on over 80% of their total snaps, and with Bowers typically in slot or wide alignments, Mayer got the matchups against linebackers and safeties from his traditional inline alignments. Throw in the fact that the Raiders' traditional wide receivers are a thin group without much demand for targets, and I still think Mayer is the second target after Bowers. As opposing defenses spend more resources to take Bowers out of the game plan, it's Mayer who will benefit. The Raiders have a good shot of a trailing game script against the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs' run-heavy approach shortens the clock and makes it a little tougher to take receptions, so I prefer receiving yards here. But if we get into a big score deficit in the second half, I'll look for a live receptions over on Mayer. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-8 -3.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 7-4 +3.6 Receiving props 5-10 -5.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 27-29 -3.4 Walder's prop bets Note: More defensive props will be added as odds become available Defensive plays Miami Dolphins to record first sack of game (+170) On one hand, this is bold because the Dolphins have not sacked the quarterback this season. Not once. On the other hand, maybe it's not that bold, because the Minnesota Vikings have taken sacks at the second-highest rate in the NFL (10.2%). Granted, that was partially with Carson Wentz in the lineup, and now Minnesota has a more mobile Kyler Murray back. But still, my belief has always been that the quarterback and offense control sacks more than the defense. I spun up a new model for this category just this week, and it seems like it agrees, considering it has the Dolphins as a plus-money value. Arizona Cardinals to NOT give up a sack on their first drive (-411) NFL Playoff Predictor Predict the final standings in every division, then choose which teams will earn a wild-card berth! FREE to play. Make Your Picks One of the biggest disappointments of the season thus far has been a New York Giants pass rush that has managed a 1.0% sack rate, second worst among all teams. Their pass rush win rate tells a similar story; it ranks 25th best. Now, the Cardinals' pass protection has also not been good this year, ranking second worst in pass block win rate. Despite that, they have allowed sacks on just 4.1% of dropbacks, better than the league average of 6.0%. My model believes their chances of giving up a sack on their opening drive is quite a bit lower than these odds suggest. Greg Rousseau under 0.75 sacks (+147) Rousseau is having an unbelievable start to the season, with 6.0 sacks in three games. It's a huge jump in sack pace for him: he's never recorded more than 8.0 sacks in a season. While Rousseau probably has improved, the model is skeptical he's improved as much as these odds imply. A big reason why? His pass rush win rate still isn't that great. A year ago Rousseau was in the 16th percentile in the metric at edge. Now, he's the 30th percentile. Better, sure, but it still suggests he isn't winning on a down-to-down basis as much as top-flight pass rushers. And that reduces his sack forecast going forward. I would bet this down to even money. Jermaine Johnson II over 0.25 sacks (+275) I've been a long-time Johnson skeptic, but this line has pushed the hate so far that I'm on his side now. One factor is the quarterback he's facing: Lamar Jackson . The Ravens' quarterback has taken sacks at an average-ish 5.7% clip this year, but my model isn't ready to totally forget the massive 9.8% number he recorded a year ago. And even if you don't think Johnson is great -- and I don't -- he's still on the field on 66% of the Titans' pass rushes and 77% in clear passing situations. This line is too good to pass up. I would bet this down to +175. Other sack bets I recommend: Arden Key over 0.25 sacks (+197) Abdul Carter over 0.25 sacks (+109) Dayo Odeyingbo under 0.25 sacks (-135) Jeffery Simmons over 0.25 sacks (+112) Donovan Ezeiruaku over 0.25 sacks (+249) Danielle Hunter under 0.75 sacks (-108) Andrew Van Ginkel under 0.75 sacks (-107) Leonard Williams under 0.75 sacks (-108) George Karlaftis over 0.25 sacks (+224) Aidan Hutchinson under 0.75 sacks (+131) Brandon Jones under 6.5 tackles + assists (+103) Jones is recording a tackle on 16% of opponent run plays and 8% of opponent pass plays. It's the first number that stands out, because it ranks in the 84th percentile among safeties. But here's the thing: the 49ers have been pass-heavy this season! They literally rank first in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. And every time a Broncos opponent opts to pass instead of run, that cuts Jones' chances of recording a tackle roughly in half. That's one reason why my model likes Jones' under quite a bit. I would bet this down to -132. Roquan Smith over 7.5 tackles + assists (+102) This is a low tackle line for Smith to clear, considering he's gone over 7.5 in each of his three games this season and nine out of 15 last year. On one hand, we can understand why: the Ravens are huge favorites over the Titans, and so the game script expectation is that Tennessee will fall behind and be forced to pass. For a linebacker like Smith, that would be bad for his tackling numbers since he's much more likely to record one against the run. But working in our favor is that Tennessee has been extremely run heavy thus far, ranking 31st in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Other tackle bets I recommend: Reed Blankenship under 6.5 tackles + assists (-117) Fred Warner under 8.5 tackles + assists (+104) Pat Surtain II under 4.5 tackles + assists (-102) Deommodore Lenoir under 5.5 tackles + assists (-124) Ji'Ayir Brown over 4.5 tackles + assists (-118) Offensive plays Jordan Love pass attempts UNDER 35.5 (-119) The Green Bay Packers have been pass-heavy in 2026, with the sixth-highest pass rate over expectation according to NFL Next Gen Stats. My attempts model assumes that is going to come down, because leaning that heavily on the pass game is not what the Packers have done in the past under Matt LaFleur. Green Bay ranked 26th in the same category last season. But there's also this: The Packers' offensive line has struggled immensely. I can only imagine they would want to limit the number of times Love drops back on Sunday, especially against Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles, who loves to blitz. Jaylen Wright receptions OVER 1.5 (+180) Wright and Ollie Gordon II will handle the backfield workload in the wake of De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL injury. Both have almost no experience catching the ball in the pros, but someone is going to have to catch passes out of the backfield -- and that's especially true this week. That's because the Miami Dolphins are playing the Minnesota Vikings, one of the most zone-heavy teams in the league (78% zone). Running backs catch passes against zone coverage almost twice as frequently compared to when they face man coverage, and in my back tests, betting the receptions over on running backs facing zone-heavy defenses has been profitable. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 88526 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). articles.description: Will Hill is back with his best bet for every NFL Week 4 game.
articles.text: 2026 NFL Week 4 Picks: Best Bets For Every Game — Will's Wagers | FOX Sports my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores Watch Betting Stories Search Sign In Account SPORTS & TEAMS PLAYERS SHOWS PERSONALITIES TOPICS POPULAR SEARCHES - No Data Available - BROWSE BY SPORTS & TEAMS PLAYERS SHOWS PERSONALITIES TOPICS Built on National Football League National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google 2026 NFL Week 4 Picks: Best Bets For Every Game — Will's Wagers Published Oct. 1, 2026 1:55 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Will Hill FOX Sports Betting Analyst There are several barnburners on tap for NFL Week 4. Here's where I'm putting my money. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins.

I have seven picks I like this week, including player props on Patrick Mahomes , Drake Maye , and Tony Pollard , plus three spreads picks for the 1 PM Eastern games. Best of luck, happy November, and enjoy your day! Vikings at Lions (-3): O/U 46.5 I said Monday of this week on NBC that this was the no-brainer of the week. It’s a miracle that the Minnesota Vikings are the lone undefeated team in the NFL, and to me, they are the most overrated team. In the last four games, Minnesota has beaten Tampa Bay, Miami, New Orleans, and Indianapolis; those teams are a combined 7-20. Last season, the Vikings swept the Lions in the regular season, and adding Kyler Murray likely doesn’t equate to another sweep over Detroit. Murray ranks 21st and 26th in passer rating against man and zone coverage, 28th in blitzed completion percentage (54.8%), and 26th in play-action completion percentage (54.9%). On early downs, Minnesota ranks in success rate, while Detroit is first. Going score for score on the road as an underdog with Jared Goff and the Lions doesn’t seem plausible to me. I like Detroit -3 at -120 odds. Pick: Lions -3 (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Titans at Bengals (-12.5): O/U 46.5 Tony Pollard had a season-high 129 rushing yards on 25 carries and tied a career-high with three rushing touchdowns. It was a great day for Pollard, but the Titans lost at the buzzer 27-24 to the Browns. Now, Tennessee goes on the road as double-digit underdogs in Cincinnati. Not a recipe for success. Last week, Pollard had an amazing game script to be fed, maybe the best he’s had all year, but I don’t see it this week, especially going up against Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen . The Bengals held Derrick Henry to 45 rushing yards on 17 carries last week, and with Cam Ward striking no fear in the Bengals’ hearts, I’d think Cincy stacks the box and attempt to take Pollard out of the equation. I went Under 65.5 rushing yards on Pollard and would go down to 60.5. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 65.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Browns at Steelers (-3.5): O/U 38.5 I still can’t believe my eyes and ears regarding the Cleveland Browns being 5-2! But all good things must come to an end, right? All five of Cleveland’s wins have come by four or fewer points, and they needed a walkoff field goal to beat the Titans in Tennessee and the same at home against the Ravens in the last two weeks. Cleveland has been playing with fire recently, while the Steelers were spotted flying back from Paris playing with ice. Aaron Rodgers was wearing chains that cost more than my house and probably yours too on that flight back from the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris. Rodgers said it was his favorite road flight of his lengthy NFL career, and the Steelers are starting to hit their stride with three-straight wins following the loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers traveling back to an immediate game is worrisome because the last eight teams that played in London, then a game in the States the following week, went 0-8 ATS! However, the Browns haven’t swept the Steelers in the regular season since 1988. It’s a revenge spot for Pittsburgh, and if you’ve seen the back-and-forth between Cam Heyward and Jared Verse this week, then you know it’s going to be a classic AFC North slugfest. Give me Pittsburgh at home -3.5. I’d prefer a -3, but the sportsbooks are playing more defense than ever this season. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (1 unit) Falcons at Bucs (-2.5): O/U Tampa Bay got that Baker bump last week! Baker Mayfield came back from injury and Tampa Bay looked inspired. The Bucs rattled Bryce Young last week and destroyed his confidence turning three turnovers into 17 of the teams 43 points. This week won’t be so easy hosting Atlanta in a letdown spot off the hype. Mayfield only threw the ball 11 times, so we truly don’t know how healthy he is or how effective he will be, but we know what to expect from Atlanta. The Falcons have the fifth-best offensive success rate since Michael Penix has taken over, and he’s gotten the ball out quick with 50% of his passes coming within 2.5 seconds (fourth-best). That could be the key against a blitz and pressure heavy Bucs defense. Tampa Bay loads the box with eight or more players at the second-highest clip (22.1%) and blitzes 40.4% of the time when doing so, which ranks fifth-most. I’d expect a lot of screens, draws, and quick throws to offeset the Bucs defense, while Atlanta likely brings pressure and tries to hit Mayfield as many times as possible to truly test his health and conditioning. Give me Atlanta. Pick: Falcons +2.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Patriots (-7) at Dolphins: O/U 43.5 Last season, Drake Maye completed 33-of-41 (80.5%) passes for 421 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions over two wins against Miami. Maye even added 72 rushing yards and another score on 15 carries in those two outings. This Miami defense is even less menacing than last year. The Dolphins have four interceptions on the season, and two came in Week 1 against Kirk Cousins , with another last week courtesy of Geno Smith . When Joe Burrow , Patrick Mahomes , Brock Purdy , and Kyler Murray played Miami, that group averaged 242.5 passing yards against the Dolphins and combined for eight touchdown passes to one interception. Kyler Murray was the only quarterback who hasn’t thrown at least two touchdowns against Miami. At -102 odds, I like Maye to go Under 0.5 Interceptions versus Miami for a third consecutive time and like 2+ Pass touchdowns for parlays. Pick: Drake Maye Under 0.5 Interceptions (1 unit) Chiefs (-1.5) at Broncos: O/U 40.5 In Week 1 against Denver, Patrick Mahomes came back from a major surgery and finished with 184 passing yards, 15-of-27 passing, and three total touchdowns, including an epic rushing score to start the game. He went Under all of his props except passing touchdowns and rushing yards. Fast forward to last week, Mahomes had his worst game of the season on Sunday Night Football against the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks in Seattle. Mahomes turns around and goes to Denver to face a Broncos defense that almost went to the Super Bowl. It’s going to be a long day for the Chiefs, but unless Kenneth Walker goes crazy again (191 total yards, 2 TDs) this looks like a spot for Mahomes to go over his props. The Broncos average 5.1 plays per possession, ranking worst in the NFL. That’s one area that points toward more plays and possessions for the Chiefs. Both of these teams rarely allow sacks or turn the ball over, so we should see plenty of possessions. Both teams had 12 drives in Week 1’s meeting, and Kansas City ran 20 more plays than Denver (62-42) thanks to the running game, and it was Davis Webb ‘s first game as an OC with the Broncos. Still, Kansas City will likely run more plays and have more possessions than Denver. Denver got back Jonathan Cooper last week, plus Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga could both play today. The Denver defense has usually limited the touchdown damage through the air from Mahomes, but in order to move the ball against Denver’s defense, Mahomes will have to be actively taking what the Broncos can give him. I like Mahomes to go Over 20.5 completions and 220.5 paassing yards up to 21.5 and 225.5. I lean his Over pass attempts. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . 49ers @ Cowboys I think wagering on a side or total for a Cowboys game is a foolish decision. You never know what you’re getting from this team. What I do know about this game is that the 49ers will use Christian McCaffrey as they normally do. CMC had 18 carries last week and an additional three targets through the air. That’s 21 attempts to gain yards in a game the Niners won by multiple touchdowns. In the last two close games the 49ers have played, CMC got 16 carries and 10 targets. I’d imagine this game will see the 49ers looking to put up some numbers, as the Cowboys' offense will probably look to do the same, since the defense can't … defend. The Dallas defense ranks 31st against the rush, and it is middle-of-the-pack in receiving yards allowed to running backs. However, Dallas doesn’t face many teams that want to pass to the running back as much as the 49ers do. Geoff Schwartz likes Christian McCaffrey to have a productive Week 10 (Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images). Schwartz's Pick: Christian McCaffrey Over 99.5 rushing and receiving yards Vikings @ Packers Can Kirk Cousins lead the Vikings past the scorching-hot Packers in his first game back with Minnesota? (David Berding/Getty Images). The Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins on Tuesday to help fix their offensive woes. He’s an immediate upgrade over what the Vikings had at QB with Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray. And while Cousins is probably average at best right now, that’s all the Vikings need at that position. The Vikings’ defense and special teams are elite. Minnesota just needs an offense that can move the ball enough to score points, so the defense doesn’t have to be perfect to win games. This move might actually allow the Vikings’ defense to play even better. The Packers have been outstanding at throwing down the field. Jordan Love has been bombing the ball to his receivers, and although the rushing game isn’t great, Green Bay is scoring enough points. The defense has also played better than expected, shutting down nearly every offense it has faced this season. I like the Vikings to cover this game for a few reasons. For starters, just having Cousins in the lineup will reinvigorate the Vikings, and it wouldn’t surprise me to see Justin Jefferson have his best game of the season. I also like the matchup of the Vikings’ defense against the Packers’ offensive line, which is mediocre. Minnesota's pressure packages will be difficult to handle. Follow on X Multiple Authors Nov 15, 2026, 04:21 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Wek 10 of the NFL season is already upon us. We've looked at the games, the odds and available props in hopes of trying to find the best value for bets. Ben Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Seth Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Matt Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's favorite bets Solak's plays | Walder's props Clay's TD projections Bowen's favorite bets We'll start with our game pick this week with the Chiefs-Falcons matchup in Atlanta. Plus, I have multiple teasers for the Week 10 slate, and I'll add a player prop on a wide receiver who is creating explosive plays at a high rate. Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons 1 p.m. ET on CBS; Line: KC -3, O/U: 46.5 Patrick Mahomes has a new target to work with as Josh Downs joins the fray against the Falcons. Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images The Chiefs added wide receiver Josh Downs at the trade deadline, giving Patrick Mahomes a slot target who can create numbers after the catch. The foot quickness is there to uncover. But I like the Chiefs to cover as a road favorite because of the run game and Steve Spagnuolo's defense. Kenneth Walker III is a difference-maker in Andy Reid's offense, averaging 23.1 touches and 130.5 scrimmage yards per game. but has been ruled out for Sunday due to a groin injury, elevating rookie Emmett Johnson to the lead role. Johnson has the vision and elusive ability to find daylight versus an Atlanta defense allowing 4.4 YPC (22nd in the league), while Reid can use the heavy run action to influence linebackers on play-action concepts. Defensively, Spagnuolo's unit will mix late rotation, Cover 2 and pressure against a Falcons offense that is lacking passing rhythm right now. And quarterback Michael Penix Jr . has struggled against the blitz this season (48.4 QBR). The Browns will need more rushing efficiency from Quinshon Judkins , but I feel comfortable with the altered spread at home because of a Cleveland pass defense that matches up well with Houston. In the other matchup in this teaser, Kyle Shanahan can scheme up a Dallas defense that is giving up 26.8 points and 372.7 yards per game. Look for play-action early with Brock Purdy targeting the seams and deep in-breakers, while the 49ers' defense creates issues for Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' passing game. Two team, 6.5-point teaser (-135): Minnesota Vikings +9.5 at Green Bay Packers , Buffalo Bills -2 at New York Jets The trade for Kirk Cousins should create more volume and production for Justin Jefferson , and that will open more daylight for the Vikings' run game. But I'm taking Minnesota, with the spread being bumped to +9.5 points, because of Brian Flores' defense. I expect more zone pressure here because of the vertical ability of both Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , but the Vikings will look to create chaos for Jordan Love . I like the Bills in the other matchup. Coach Joe Brady will have pressure answers for Josh Allen to get the ball out (catch-and-run targets for DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir ), and don't be surprised if the Bills lead with a run-heavy approach to control tempo. Jameson Williams longest reception OVER 24.5 yards (-112) Williams has had a reception of 24 or more yards in five straight games. With his vertical ability, plus the dynamic open-field speed he displays after the catch, I like Williams to hit the over against New England. I love the Steelers' potential to keep this game close because they have the sort of ball-control, run-heavy offense that can minimize the number of possessions Joe Burrow gets in this game. Since Week 3, when Pittsburgh rejiggered the right side of its offensive line, the Steelers are third in success rate and first in EPA on rushing snaps; no team has a higher explosive run rate, and it isn't close. When they faced the Bengals in Week 3, Jaylen Warren had 17 carries for 127 yards. Now, Rico Dowdle is back to help. The Steelers are also big on targeting the backs and tight ends in the passing game, which is where you want to go after this Bengals defense, and the lingering ankle injury to DJ Turner II also makes Cincinnati fairly weak in the secondary. It's a divisional game, and the Bengals are too hot and cold to trust with more than a field goal against a Steelers team off the bye. Rico Dowdle receiving yards OVER 13.5 (-114) Editor's Picks Joe Burrow is the NFL MVP favorite, but is he the best bet? Pamela Maldonado Early bets for NFL Week 10: Two games we're jumping on now ESPN NFL Week 10 betting odds for every game ESPN 2 Related Dowdle returned to the Steelers' lineup in Week 6 and had seven routes to Warren's 27 in that game against the Buccaneers. But he was targeted on four of those seven routes, and since then has 24 routes and six targets to Warren's 22 routes and six targets. The receiving volume has been fairly split since his return, and rightfully so -- Warren has been an exceptional between-the-tackles runner this season, and Dowdle has always been a capable pass catcher. Yet, Warren is projected for 25.5 yards and 3.5 receptions, whereas Dowdle is at 13.5 and 2.5. Given how willingly Aaron Rodgers targets the backs and how poor the Bengals' linebackers are in coverage and at tackling in the open field, backfield receiving production should be a strong part of Pittsburgh's offensive approach, and Dowdle is the far cheaper option in what should be near a 50/50 opportunity split. Keep an eye on this number live. If Warren starts out the first quarter taking most of the snaps on a couple of Pittsburgh three-and-outs, Dowdle's numbers will drop even more, and I'll start looking for live alts. Tutu Atwell receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-109) It's worth wondering just who it is that is going to catch passes for the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua -- who had 19 targets and 14 receptions on 43 routes last week against the Commanders -- joins Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington on the injured reserve bench. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also probably out for Sunday's game at Arizona. The two primary route runners behind Nacua at receiver last Sunday were Konata Mumpfield and Atwell, the latter of whom was targeted five times for two receptions and 16 yards. Atwell ended the day with 37 unrealized air yards -- that is to say, he had 53 air yards to the 16 receiving yards he actually produced. In back-to-back weeks, he has had at least 50 air yards on 17 and 20 routes, respectively. Given the thinness of the Rams' receiver room, 20 routes should be a floor projection for Atwell, as long as the Cardinals' offense can keep things competitive with Carson Beck under center. Even if they can't, Atwell's downfield usage can get us home on one big reception. If you're looking to get really frisky in what should be a sleepy late afternoon game, Rams rookie receiver CJ Daniels to score a touchdown is +950. He's a big-framed receiver, which the Rams will need behind the smaller Mumpfield and Atwell. Worth a sprinkle! Tre Tucker receiving yards OVER 25.5 (-115) NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Tucker is tied for ninth in targets of at least 20 air yards but has only a 35.7% receptions rate, thanks in large part to six of those 14 targets landing inaccurate with quarterback Kirk Cousins . Cousins, for as good as he was at the helm of the Raiders' offense, lacks a deep-ball arm at this stage of his career. With rookie Fernando Mendoza ready to start his first career game, I expect the Raiders' passing attack to become less incremental and a bit more vertical, which speaks to Tucker's game. Though the matchup against the Seattle Seahawks ' defense is certainly an intimidating one for a green passer, Klint Kubiak is well suited to find space against this defense -- he saw it work for a whole season up close when he was the coordinator in Seattle last season. I'm confident he'll have a trick or two up his sleeve. I wouldn't usually take a receiving over against this Seahawks defense that leads the league in yards per target allowed to opposing wideouts. But the number is too low for a primary receiver and can be reached on one big play. I'll be on alts as well for this bet, and we also will track 40-plus yards for a half unit at +194. Geno Smith passing yards OVER 220.5 (-113) The Buffalo Bills ' defense has enjoyed two softer quarterback matchups after their bye. Against the Ravens, both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down, forcing emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano into the game. Against the Vikings, it was backup Carson Wentz . Perhaps something seriously improved in the Bills' secondary post-bye -- and they are adding safety Amani Hooker , a nice deadline addition, at safety -- but before that bye, opposing quarterbacks were ripping through Buffalo's pass defense. Cousins had 313 yards in Week 6, Matthew Stafford had 383 in Week 5, and Drake Maye had 269 in Week 4. The Bills are rightfully large favorites over the 2-7 New York Jets , who probably will run the ball early in an attempt to keep it close, then eventually get forced into a pass-heavy script. Smith has cleared this number in three of his past four games and is 11th in the league in yards per pass attempt. When the Jets have to throw, he puts up big numbers. With Garrett Wilson expected to return from the concussion protocol, the Jets' receiver trio is at full force, and Smith should produce accordingly. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Daniel Jones passing yards UNDER 186.5 (-112) The Indianapolis Colts receiver room is as bad as any I can think of in the past 10 years of non-COVID football. With Downs and Keenan Allen both traded at the deadline, the Colts are fielding Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin and Deion Burks as starting wideouts. Indianapolis retained running back Jonathan Taylor at the trade deadline, so it's fair to expect the Colts to increase their reliance on the handoff game. The Miami Dolphins ' passing defense gives up the third-most yards per pass attempt in the league but gives up only 198.4 yards per game, right around league average. That's because nobody needs to throw it against them to win. Especially with defensive tackle Zach Sieler now hurt, the Colts should be able to run the ball with plenty of success. This Colts' passing attack is as below league average as it gets, and with Malik Willis out, the likelihood the Dolphins get a second-half lead and force a pass-happy approach is greatly diminished. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-8 -3.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 7-4 +3.6 Receiving props 5-10 -5.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 27-29 -3.4 Walder's prop bets Defensive plays Indianapolis Colts D/ST Anytime TD (+550) This is straightforward: We're trying to capitalize on Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord making his NFL debut. Is the Colts' defense good? It is not. But it almost doesn't matter. Indianapolis is a 3.5-point favorite, and the chances of a disastrous mistake from McCord is elevated given his status as a former sixth-round pick who has never taken a pro snap in a regular-season game. My model, which is making those quite negative assumptions about McCord, prices this at +450. New England Patriots to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-391) The Patriots are light underdogs this week against the Detroit Lions , who do boast the second-best pass rush win rate this season. But the Patriots are third best in pass block win rate, which, along with Drake Maye 's average sack rate, is why my model isn't overly concerned about Maye falling to a first-drive sack. At least not at this price, anyway. I make the fair line -514. Chase Young under 0.75 sacks (+158) Believe it or not Young is tied for second in the NFL in sacks with 8.0 (only behind Will Anderson Jr .) and this line is absolutely a reflection of that. I generally consider myself a Chase Young backer -- because after the early disappointment of his career he quickly became underrated - but wow has this gone too far. In fact, if the line closes at this price it would be the strongest sack prop line of the year. There is no way Young - whose pass rush win rate is above average but still just in the 69th percentile - is on that kind of level. Chop Robinson over 0.25 sacks (+132) This will be the fifth time I've bet Robinson's sack over in this year's column and it doesn't look like we'll be slowing down any time soon (we're 2-2 and +1.1 units thus far). Robinson is the league leader in pass rush win rate at edge. Let me say that again: he is the league leader in pass rush win rate at edge. And to back it up: he leads edge rushers in pressure rate, too! That's multiple forms of measurement coming away with the same conclusion: on a down-to-down basis Robinson is consistently beating his blocker and causing problems for the quarterback. That it's only resulted in 4.0 sacks is why we still get to bet it at this price. And this week, we get an added bonus: the Dolphins aren't even that big underdogs this week (+4.5 at the Colts). Two years ago he recorded a tackle rate on run plays that ranked in the 94th percentile among interior linemen with at least 300 snaps played, along with a 97th percentile run stop win rate. But he is not the same player now at age 33. Among defensive tackles with 200 snaps plays this year Stewart ranks in the 63rd percentile in tackle rate against the run and the 12th percentile in run stop win rate. Even against the run-heavy Dolphins my model believes this line is a little too optimistic for Stewart. Bryan Cook under 6.5 tackles + assists (-149) This is an increased line from where Cook has been in the past couple of weeks after he went over this number twice in the last three games (though those are the only two times he's gone over this line all year). Only 29% of tackle lines on safeties this year have been 6.5 or higher, and I'm not sure Cook ought to be quite on that level even with this number shaded under. Cook ranks in the 82nd percentile in tackle rate vs. the pass but just 38th percentile against the run, but those equate to nearly equal tackling rates so I don't think game script is a huge factor here. Overall, my model thinks this line is a little high. Running backs record a reception on 8% dropbacks against man coverage but 15% against zone. And based on back-testing research, I don't believe this fact is fully baked into reception lines. The last couple of weeks I've used this information to bet the under on running backs facing man-heavy defenses -- we hit on Alvin Kamara 's under last week -- but this time I'm flipping the script and opting for Brown's over against the Steelers. Pittsburgh is the heaviest zone coverage team in the NFL, running zone 79% of the time. The Big Game has become a full menu of prop markets that attract both casual fans and seasoned bettors. From the opening coin toss to the l ength of the national anthem , and even the color of the post-game Gatorade shower , novelty wagers have become a major part of the experience and consistently draw heavy interest leading up to kickoff. Below, we break down some of the most popular Super Bowl props along with how they've performed historically, also providing some of our expert's predictions on whether the Seattle Seahawks or New England Patriots will lift the Lombardi Trophy. All odds below were taken from FanDuel Sportsbook as of Feb. 7. Let's take a look: Super Bowl LX odds Seahawks vs. Patriots Spread: Seahawks -4.5 Moneyline: Seahawks -235, Patriots +194 O/U: 45.5 Super Bowl LX MVP odds Sam Darnold : +115 (bet $10 to win $21.50 total) Drake Maye : +230 (bet $10 to win $33 total) Jaxon Smith-Njigba : +550 (bet $10 to win $65 total) Kenneth Walker III : +850 (bet $10 to win $95 total) Rhamondre Stevenson : +3000 (bet $10 to win $410 total) Rashid Shaheed : +3000 (bet $10 to win $310 total) Stefon Diggs : +4000 (bet $10 to win $410 total) This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. Expert Predictions Will Hill : Seahawks 27, Patriots 17 The Patriots have had a remarkable turnaround post-Bill Belichick, but the Seahawks will pose a significant step-up in competition compared to what the AFC bracket presented. I expect a low-scoring game, but I think the more talented Seahawks will ultimately pull away and win 27-17, with Sam Darnold taking home MVP. Chris Fallica : Seahawks 27, Patriots 23 I hate the game from a spread standpoint. It seems like a simple handicap where Seattle is better at every position group, and groupthink has the Seahawks winning comfortably. If anything, I’ll see if I can get a cheap Seahawks moneyline on the game, but I’m not going to lay 4.5 here. Sammy P : Seahawks 23, Patriots 20 After a low-scoring first quarter, I expect things to stay competitive the rest of the way. New England (15-5 ATS) made bettors money all season long and that mostly came in the favorite role. Mike Vrabel is a tremendous underdog coach and that song should remain the same this Sunday in Santa Clara. Geoff Schwartz : Seahawks 24, Patriots 13 I have the game 24-13 for the Seahawks. The Seahawks have been the best team wire-to-wire this season and the best case for the Patriots in this game is Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold turning back into a pumpkin, which I don't expect. He's been nails this postseason. The Seattle defense is going to sit in zone coverage and force New England to work for all its yards, which is difficult without dynamic playmakers at the skill positions. The Seahawks win this game comfortably. National Anthem For years, sports fans have bet on the length of the Star Spangled Banner, among other anthem-related props. Read all of his NFL Week 10 picks and predictions . Patriots vs. Lions Preview & Picks Erickson's pick: Patriots ML The Lions defense is playing better: DET has won three straight games (GB, MIN, MIA) without scoring more than 20 points for the first time since Weeks 5-8, 1974 (Next Gen Stats). Detroit’s defense is allowing 15.5 points per game since Week 5, second-best in the NFL, after allowing 31.8 points per game through the first four weeks, which ranked second-worst in the NFL. The Lions have allowed 21 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time since Weeks 7-15, 2016 (eight straight games). The Lions’ defense has allowed a 38.2% completion percentage on downfield passes since Brian Branch made his 2026 season debut in Week 7, the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL over that span (NGS). The Lions also defend what Drake Maye does best… off-script plays and extended dropbacks. The Lions’ defense has allowed just four completions for 123 yards, a touchdown, and an interception when quarterbacks have held onto the ball for at least four seconds after the snap this season (i.e., extended dropbacks), resulting in a league-low 15.4% completion percentage. Maye has recorded a league-high 46.8% success rate when holding the ball for at least four seconds after the snap this season (i.e., extended dropbacks), the highest rate by a qualified quarterback in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). Detroit has also recorded a sack on 19 of its 45 extended dropbacks faced (42.2%), the second-highest sack rate in the NFL behind only the Steelers (52.8%). Detroit has allowed just four total successful plays on extended dropbacks, resulting in a league-low 8.9% success rate, the lowest rate allowed by a defense in a season during the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016). Could go either way with the side, as I’ve contemplated both the Patriots and Lions winning. The Pats rebounding off a big loss was my early lean, but I’m acknowledging DET might not be as bad defensively. Therefore, that variable has entered into my handicap of this overseas contest. Still…hardly a murderer’s row of offenses DET has faced outside of GB (also a divisional matchup where points were left on the cutting room floor). A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson also seem like they actually might play. Because I think this game is really closer to a pick ’em…I’ll take my chances with NE on the moneyline. Mike Vrabel’s team tends to bounce back after losses – 5-1 ATS after a loss since 2025. 6-0 SU after a loss. So although I felt on the Week 10 Predictions Tailgate podcast that DET could smoke NE…I think I was letting recency bias take over. Pat Fitzmaurice talked more sense into me with backing NE as the sharp side here. Subscribe to the Tailgate Podcast here (help us get to 3K). Amon-Ra St. Brown leads all wide receivers in red-zone targets per game, and New England allows the 6th-most receiving touchdowns (14 this season). This is a homecoming for St. Brown. His mother is from Germany; he has dual citizenship in Germany and the United States, and he speaks fluent German. He has not scored since Week 3, so I think he is due. Look for the Lions to dial up some red-zone plays for St. Brown to hit paydirt. An NFL player prop bet is a type of wager where you’re betting on the performance of a specific player in a game rather than the overall outcome. For example, you might place a bet on how many passing yards a quarterback will throw for, or how many touchdowns a running back will score. It’s a fun way to get more invested in the action, especially if you’re confident in how a particular player will perform, regardless of who wins or loses the game. Analyst picks and parlay prices below reflect the source articles and may differ from the matchup odds above. Here are Andrew Erickson's predictions for Patriots vs. Lions. Read all of his NFL Week 10 picks and predictions.

Patriots vs. Lions Preview & Picks Erickson's pick: Patriots ML The Lions defense is playing better: DET has won three straight games (GB, MIN, MIA) without scoring more than 20 points for the first time since Weeks 5-8, 1974 (Next Gen Stats). Detroit’s defense is allowing 15.5 points per game since Week 5, second-best in the NFL, after allowing 31.8 points per game through the first four weeks, which ranked second-worst in the NFL. The Lions have allowed 21 or fewer points in four straight games for the first time since Weeks 7-15, 2016 (eight straight games). The Lions’ defense has allowed a 38.2% completion percentage on downfield passes since Brian Branch made his 2026 season debut in Week 7, the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL over that span (NGS). The Lions also defend what Drake Maye does best... off-script plays and extended dropbacks.

Still...hardly a murderer’s row of offenses DET has faced outside of GB (also a divisional matchup where points were left on the cutting room floor). A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson also seem like they actually might play. Because I think this game is really closer to a pick ’em... I’ll take my chances with NE on the moneyline. Mike Vrabel’s team tends to bounce back after losses – 5-1 ATS after a loss since 2025. 6-0 SU after a loss. So although I felt on the Week 10 Predictions Tailgate podcast that DET could smoke NE... I think I was letting recency bias take over. Pat Fitzmaurice talked more sense into me with backing NE as the sharp side here. Subscribe to the Tailgate Podcast here (help us get to 3K). Amon-Ra St. Brown leads all wide receivers in red-zone targets per game, and New England allows the 6th-most receiving touchdowns (14 this season).

NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds.
