articles.description: Sean Barnard provides the top player prop bets for the NFL's Week 5 Monday Night Football matchup between the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.text: Bills at Rams NFL Player Prop Bets for Monday Night Football Betting Picks Fantasy Advice --> --> Betting Picks Fantasy Advice Betting Picks All Sports Betting Picks NFL Picks NBA Picks MLB Picks NHL Picks College Football Picks College Basketball Picks Soccer Picks Golf Picks UFC Picks WNBA Picks Tennis Picks NASCAR Picks Boxing Picks Fantasy Advice All Fantasy Advice NFL Fantasy NBA Fantasy MLB Fantasy NHL Fantasy Golf Fantasy UFC Fantasy WNBA Fantasy NASCAR Fantasy Pick6 Season Long Best Ball Sports NFL NBA MLB NHL College Football College Basketball Soccer Golf UFC WNBA NASCAR Tennis Boxing Wrestling Betting Tools Betting Splits Most Bet Player Props Parlays Odds, Lines & Spreads NFL Player Prop Trends Tracker NBA Player Prop Trends Tracker MLB Player Prop Trends Tracker NRFI Tracker NFL Trending Parlay Picks Optimizer News & More News Sportsbook Insights How to Watch Podcasts DKN Shows How to Bet Jackpocket Casino Entertainment All Entertainment TV & Film Movie Reviews Marvel Cinematic Universe Star Wars Pro Wrestling Trading Cards Sneaker Drops DKN Español Settings Toggle dark mode Dark Mode Betting Splits Player Props NFL Parlay Builder Sports Betting Picks Fantasy Advice Start/Sit Advice NBA Parlay Builder NFL SGP Betting Tool Parlays Odds, Lines & Spreads Entertainment DKN Español > --> Home NFL Bills at Rams NFL Player Prop Bets for Monday Night Football Buffalo Bills Sports Betting Picks NFL DraftKings Sportsbook Insights Player Props Updated: October 12, 2026 By: Sean Barnard ES Leer en español In the Week 5 NFL Monday night matchup, the Buffalo Bills will take on the Los Angeles Rams to close out the week. Both sides hold legitimate Super Bowl aspirations this season. The Bills have jumped to a 3-1 start, but they’re looking to bounce back from their first loss to the Patriots last week. On the other side, the Rams have slipped to 2-2 but still have their season goals in sight if they can find their form. This will be a notable measuring-stick matchup for both sides. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> Looking at the odds, the Rams enter as 3.5-point favorites with -175 moneyline odds on DraftKings Sportsbook . The Bills hold +145 odds to pull off the upset, with the game total set at 54.5 points. There are plenty of ways to get involved beyond just backing a side or total. Let’s take a look at my top three favorite player props for the Week 5 Monday Night Football matchup. RELATED DraftKings King of the End Zone Picks for Bills vs. Rams Monday Night Football Game Bills at Rams NFL Player Prop Bets for Monday Night Football James Cook III Over 75.5 Rushing Yards (-111) After leading the NFL in rushing yards last year with 1,621 yards, or 95.4 yards per game, James Cook III has been a bit underutilized in the Bills’ offense to start the season. Even still, the three-time Pro Bowler has tallied 70 rush attempts for 421 rushing yards and three touchdowns. He has finished with rushing totals of 57, 135, 154 and 75 yards across the first four games. Cook is recording an impressive 6.0 yards per carry this season, and he has cleared 130 yards in both games that he saw over 20 carries. This is a matchup he should be expected to get his opportunities with the ball. While Los Angeles ranks eighth in the NFL in opponent points allowed and has given up the fewest total yards in football, the Rams rank 12th in total rushing yards allowed, 13th in net yards per rush attempts and 14th in EPA per rushing play. In contrast, Los Angeles ranks first in total passing yards allowed, first in net yards per pass attempt and third in EPA per pass play. It has not been an issue of production, but opportunity thus far for Cook. He recorded 75 rushing yards on just 12 carries last week, but it is in Buffalo’s best interest to get him more involved tonight. The Philadelphia Eagles rushed for 104 yards on the ground last week, even after Saquon Barkley suffered an injury on the first drive, and the 49ers gashed Los Angeles for 174 rushing yards in the opener. Josh Allen is the headliner of the offense, but Cook is vital to this team hitting its peak. Expect a focused effort to put the ball in the 27-year-old’s hands and for 75.5 rushing yards to be a comfortable bar to clear for the third time this year. Tyler Higbee Over 2.5 Receptions (-114) While Puka Nacua and Davante Adams headline the passing attack for Los Angeles, this Rams offensive system is extremely dependent on tight end production. This is especially the case with both Nacua and Adams already banged up and dealing with some injuries. As Matthew Stafford’s supporting cast has been in and out of the blue tent, Tyler Higbee has established himself as a point of stability in the offensive attack. Through the opening four games of the season, Higbee has tallied 15 receptions on 19 targets for 141 yards and a touchdown. He has especially come alive these past two weeks. Higbee tallied eight receptions on 11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown against the Broncos and five receptions on six targets for 67 yards last week against the Eagles over the past two games. Buffalo will not provide the same level of resistance as either of these teams. The Bills enter this week ranked 25th in opponent points allowed, 27th in total yards conceded and 30th in total passing yards surrendered. Buffalo is allowing 5.4 receptions per game to the tight end position thus far. Los Angeles leans on multiple tight ends in the flow of its offensive attack. While Colby Parkinson will return from injury tonight, Terrance Ferguson remains sidelined, and there is room for each to produce regardless. Don’t expect the personnel change to mean Higbee’s standing in the offense is completely forgotten. Ferguson has just 18 career catches across 17 games played while Parkinson has three receptions on five targets across his three games played this year. Even with the collective pass-catching group getting healthier, Higbee has tallied 17 targets and 13 catches over the past two weeks, and this is a level of volume I cannot fully overlook. Expect Stafford to continue looking his way in key spots over the middle and for Higbee to comfortably clear over 2.5 receptions for the third straight week. Matthew Stafford Over 2.5 Passing Touchdowns (+128) Speaking of the man responsible for getting Higbee the football, this is a great matchup for Stafford to add to his statistical totals. It has been an up-and-down start to the year for the reigning MVP. Through his first four games, Stafford has thrown for 1,189 passing yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. He struggled greatly in the season opener, being limited to 155 passing yards and an interception against the 49ers. Stafford has thrown for 317+ yards in each of the three games since, throwing for four, two and zero touchdowns while tossing five interceptions across this stretch. In search of a get-right spot, this Buffalo defense is a great place to look. The Bills have allowed 29+ points in three of their four games this season. They enter this week ranking 25th in points allowed, 27th in total yards conceded, 30th in opponent passing yards, 29th in opponent passing touchdowns and 22nd in net yards per pass attempt. This is especially notable as the Bills currently rank 10th in rushing touchdowns allowed. A struggling Drake Maye ripped off 269 passing yards and three touchdowns last week, and Jared Goff recorded four passing scores against this Bills secondary already this year. Stafford led the NFL with 46 passing touchdowns last year, averaging 2.7 passing touchdowns per game and recording over 2.5 passing scores in nine of his 17 starts. He has still tallied as many as four passing scores in a game this season, and this is among the most favorable of a matchup he could ask for. The 54.5-point game total indicates that we should buckle up for a bit of a shootout in this game. Count on Stafford taking this responsibility upon himself to drive the offense and return to the MVP level that he has proven to be capable of playing at. Expect the matchup with Allen to bring out the best in the Rams star and for three passing scores to be a comfortable bar to clear for the second time this season. yep.title: Bills at Rams NFL Player Prop Bets for Monday Night Football
yep.description: Sean Barnard provides the top player prop bets for the NFL's Week 5 Monday Night Football matchup between the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams.
highlights: Bills at Rams NFL Player Prop Bets for Monday Night Football In the Week 5 NFL Monday night matchup, the Buffalo Bills will take on the Los Angeles Rams to close out the week. Both sides hold legitimate Super Bowl aspirations this season. The Bills have jumped to a 3-1 start, but they’re looking to bounce back from their first loss to the Patriots last week. On the other side, the Rams have slipped to 2-2 but still have their season goals in sight if they can find their form. This will be a notable measuring-stick matchup for both sides. Looking at the odds, the Rams enter as 3.5-point favorites with -175 moneyline odds on DraftKings Sportsbook. The Bills hold +145 odds to pull off the upset, with the game total set at 54.5 points. There are plenty of ways to get involved beyond just backing a side or total. Let’s take a look at my top three favorite player props for the Week 5 Monday Night Football matchup. Bills at Rams NFL Player Prop Bets for Monday Night Football

While Los Angeles ranks eighth in the NFL in opponent points allowed and has given up the fewest total yards in football, the Rams rank 12th in total rushing yards allowed, 13th in net yards per rush attempts and 14th in EPA per rushing play. In contrast, Los Angeles ranks first in total passing yards allowed, first in net yards per pass attempt and third in EPA per pass play. It has not been an issue of production, but opportunity thus far for Cook. He recorded 75 rushing yards on just 12 carries last week, but it is in Buffalo’s best interest to get him more involved tonight. The Philadelphia Eagles rushed for 104 yards on the ground last week, even after Saquon Barkley suffered an injury on the first drive, and the 49ers gashed Los Angeles for 174 rushing yards in the opener. Josh Allen is the headliner of the offense, but Cook is vital to this team hitting its peak. Expect a focused effort to put the ball in the 27-year-old’s hands and for 75.5 rushing yards to be a comfortable bar to clear for the third time this year.

James Cook III Over 75.5 Rushing Yards (-111) After leading the NFL in rushing yards last year with 1,621 yards, or 95.4 yards per game, James Cook III has been a bit underutilized in the Bills’ offense to start the season. Even still, the three-time Pro Bowler has tallied 70 rush attempts for 421 rushing yards and three touchdowns. He has finished with rushing totals of 57, 135, 154 and 75 yards across the first four games. Cook is recording an impressive 6.0 yards per carry this season, and he has cleared 130 yards in both games that he saw over 20 carries. This is a matchup he should be expected to get his opportunities with the ball.

Sign up Odds by Videos Columns Leagues MLB NFL NBA College Football College Basketball MLB NFL NBA College Football College Basketball Odds NFL NBA MLB NHL College Football College Basketball Premier League WNBA NFL NBA MLB NHL College Football College Basketball Premier League WNBA 2026 NFL Week 10 Best Bets, Picks, Predictions, Player Props, Odds: Lions vs Patriots, Steelers vs Bengals By Vaughn Dalzell , By Vaughn Dalzell Published November 12, 2026 11:31 PM Facebook Twitter Email Week 10 started with a thriller on Thursday Night Football between the Commanders and Giants! After favorites wrecked Week 9, the underdogs got out to an early win. I have three early picks for primetime games in Germany, Cincinnati, and Baltimore. Best of luck and enjoy the weekend! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. Picks: Jared Goff Over 34.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Drake Maye Over 33.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Maye over 1.5 Pass TDs (1 unit) Chiefs (-3) at Falcons: O/U 47.5 No Kenneth Walker opens the door for Patrick Mahomes to have a day. The Falcons’ opponents have the ninth-highest pass rate over exception this season, and it’s third if you remove the Buccaneers game where Baker Mayfield threw three times in a monsoon. Atlanta is allowing 228.0 passing yards per game, but remove that Mayfield performance and the number rises to 271.3, which would rank last in the NFL. Here is the list of quarterbacks and how they’ve performed this season against Atlanta. Joe Burrow: 271 Baker Mayfield: 0 Brock Purdy: 288 Caleb Williams: 305 Tyler Huntley: 201 Tyler Shough: 286 Jordan Love: 312 Bryce Young: 287 Aaron Rodgers: 221 Six out of nine quarterbacks went over 240 passing yards, including three of the last four, and six of the past eight. Mahomes has thrown for at least 240 passing yards in five of eight games and two straight. Emmett Johnson has a surprising rushing prop of 71.5 and a rush + rec prop of 102.5, so he may get a heavy dosage, but in a dome setting, I think Kansas City reverts to trusting Mahomes more. I think he adds another to his resume in Atlanta. I’d go up to 244.5. This prop was 236.5 yesterday. Pick: Patrick Mahomes 240+ Passing Yards (1 unit) Jaguars (-10.5) at Titans: O/U 46.5 I lost on Tony Pollard ‘s under rushing yards last week against the Bengals, but will run it back on his Under. Pollard has 129 and 117 rushing yards in back-to-back games on 25 and 21 carries, plus five touchdowns. Both game scripts worked out that Tennessee was in the game until the final whistle, so running the ball was never out of the question. However, that could change here. Not only could the bye week throw off the ground game’s rhythm, but this matchup is the toughest of the season on paper. In the last three games, Derrick Henry was held to 57 rushing yards last week, and Jonathan Taylor to 23 yards two weeks ago, plus Woody Marks had 56 yards. Jacksonville ranks fifth in the NFL with 89.3 rushing yards allowed per game, but that also dropped after Justice Hill had a garbage-time 65-yard run last week. Pollard has hit the over in three straight games and is 5-3 to the over on the season. I’m buying into regression hitting this week. I’m taking the under 58.5 rushing yards down to 53.5. I expect a negative game script and Pollard’s role in the pass game to increase here, and his carries regress back to the norm. Last season, Pollard ran for 60 and 48 yards against the Jaguars on 10 and 14 carries. Jacksonville won by 22 and 34 points. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 58.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Vikings at Packers (-3): O/U 42.5 Did you know that Jordan Love is the only quarterback to throw for two touchdowns against the Vikings this season? That was in Week 1, so seven-straight quarterbacks have thrown for one or fewer touchdowns against Minnesota. Well, fast forward to Week 10, and Green Bay still doesn’t have a running game, so Love has carried the offense. If the Packers are to score more than two touchdowns in this game, it’s hard for me to see it not coming from the arm of Love. He is 8-1 to the over 1.5 passing touchdowns this season. I’ll take him to go Over 1.5 passing touchdowns against Minnesota again and ride his heater of three-straight overs. Outside boundary receivers have had a hard time against Minnesota this season, but one wideout that burned the Vikings defense was Matthew Golden . He’s burned me too. I faded Golden the past two weeks, and he snuck over with 79 yards, then had a monster 164 yards against New England. This becomes a fade spot of a career-high and after catching all 10 targets. I am going under 71.5 yards on Golden, down to 66.5. I’ll root for a red zone touchdown from him, though. Picks: Jordan Love Over 1.5 Passing TDs (1 unit), Matthew Golden Under 71.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Steelers at Bengals (-3.5): O/U 49.5 It may be November, but this game will feel like a December or January clash with playoff implications. The Steelers and Bengals are both on four-game winning streaks, and the winner will be in first place in the AFC North. The spread and total for this first game were Bengals -3.5 and 42.5, so we have a full seven-point correction on the total for the second game after Pittsburgh won 30-27 in Week 3. Pittsburgh has been money in years past with Mike Tomlin coming off a bye week (17-5 ML), but this Mike McCarthy’s team now, plus the Bengals, are incredible when at a rest disadvantage. Since 2019 with Zac Taylor , the Bengals are 18-5-1 ATS with a rest disadvantage. Rather than picking a side, I am going under 24.5 points in the first half. The first-half score was 17-17 in Week 3 and flew over the 20.5 first-half total. There could be a lack of rhythm early coming out of the break for the Steelers, and it’ll be hard for the Bengals to replicate or improve on their 7.1-yard play last week against Atlanta. Plus, the Bengals are going off an overseas game, which is never easy on the body. With the intensity of this game early, I like the first half under 24.5 points. Neither team has played anybody good while lighting it up during their four-game win streaks, so the defenses may surprise us. Pick: Steelers vs Bengals 1H Under 24.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Chargers at Ravens (-4.5): O/U 38.5 If you were the Chargers and had to pick an opponent, you’d be picking from the Colts, Dolphins, Eagles, and Ravens at this point (LA lost to the Raiders and Cardinals). This is as good of a matchup for the Chargers offense as it gets. Baltimore has allowed 33-plus points in three straight games, and it might not get better with questionable tags to three starting defensive backs. This is also the Chargers’ first primetime game of the season and first of two or three (Week 15 could get flexed). I think Los Angeles will want this game a little more, and Jim Harbaugh might call up his brother John for any secrets to pull off the win against his former Ravens team. It doesn’t scare me that Jacoby Brissett will be making his Ravens debut in Baltimore on Monday Night Football, because, like I said, that Ravens’ defense has some serious issues. The Chargers finally found the end zone last week after 37 straight drives without a touchdown, and I think they’ll find it more than once in Baltimore. I like the Chargers to get the first cover of the season (0-7-1 ATS), and I think they can win too. Baltimore is 0-4 ATS at home (worst) and 2-7 ATS this season (third-worst). I will take L.A. +4.5. Best NFL Player Props for Thursday Night Football: Panthers vs. Packers Through Week 6, the Packers had a 7.8% pass rate over expected (PROE). In Josh Jacobs’ Week 7 return, Green Bay had a 6.4% PROE. It was a small step back, but it was something. Meanwhile, Carolina’s defense ranks 29th in PROE against (-2.6%) this season, and they were just curbstomped by Tampa Bay’s rushing attack. Tampa Bay’s trio of Bucky Irving, Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker rumbled for 246 yards and 5.47 yards per carry. It was the second time a team’s backfield exceeded 200 rushing yards against the Panthers this season. Carolina has allowed the most rushing yards per game (126.8) and yards per carry (5.21) to running backs this season. D’Andre Swift (124 rushing yards), Irving (106 rushing yards), Kyle Monangai (100 rushing yards), Gainwell (88 rushing yards), Bijan Robinson (72 rushing yards) and Quinshon Judkins (70 rushing yards) each surpassed 59.5 rushing yards against the Panthers this season. Jacobs is once again the Packers’ lead back. In his first game of the season, he handled 11 of Green Bay’s backfield’s 17 rush attempts (64.7%). Jacobs managed only 36 rushing yards on 11 carries for 3.27 yards per carry. Nevertheless, his workload was rock-solid, and if he shook off some rust, he could be more efficient and take a larger piece of the pie against Carolina’s pitiful run defense. Jacobs topped 59.5 rushing yards in nine of 16 games last season, and he should clear the over on Thursday for the first time this season. An NFL player prop bet is a type of wager where you’re betting on the performance of a specific player in a game rather than the overall outcome. For example, you might place a bet on how many passing yards a quarterback will throw for, or how many touchdowns a running back will score. It’s a fun way to get more invested in the action, especially if you’re confident in how a particular player will perform, regardless of who wins or loses the game. It’s like focusing on one slice of the pie instead of the whole thing.
